ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a square, with two tangent circles inside. The upper-left circle is tangent to both the top side and the left side of the square, and its upper point of tangency is labeled A; the lower-right circle is tangent to both the bottom side and the right side of the square, and its right-side point of tangency is labeled B. The two circles are tangent near the diagonal of the square, and the point of tangency is labeled O; red line segments connect A to O and O to B, and angle AOB is required. Reasoning: Using the coordinate method, let the side length of the square be s and the radius of the circles be r. Take the lower-left corner of the square as (0,0), and the upper-right corner as (s,s). The center of the upper-left circle is C1=(r,s-r), and its top-side point of tangency is A=(r,s). The center of the lower-right circle is C2=(s-r,r), and its right-side point of tangency is B=(s,r). The two circles are externally tangent, so C1C2=2r. From the coordinates, C1C2=sqrt((s-2r)^2+(s-2r)^2)=sqrt(2)(s-2r), therefore sqrt(2)(s-2r)=2r. The point of tangency O is the midpoint of the line connecting the two circle centers, so O=(s/2,s/2). Thus vector OA=(r-s/2,s/2), OB=(s/2,r-s/2). Let t=s/2-r, then OA=(-t,s/2), OB=(s/2,-t). From sqrt(2)(s-2r)=2r, that is sqrt(2)·2t=2r, we get sqrt(2)t=r=s/2-t, so t/(s/2)=sqrt(2)-1=tan 22.5°. Therefore the direction angle of OA is 112.5°, the direction angle of OB is -22.5°, and the angle between them is 112.5°-(-22.5°)=135°.

raw_record.question_text: Two circles are tangent to each other and also to two sides of a square. As shown in the figure, what is the measure of angle $A\hat{O}B$ determined by three of these points of tangency?

method.method_draft: Use a coordinate/radius setup from the diagram. First read the image: a square contains two congruent-looking circles placed in opposite corners; the upper-left circle is tangent to the top and left sides, the lower-right circle is tangent to the bottom and right sides, the circles touch at point O on the square diagonal, A is the top tangency point of the upper-left circle, and B is the right tangency point of the lower-right circle. Let the square have side length s and each circle have radius r. Put the square corners at (0,0) and (s,s). Then the upper-left circle center is C1=(r,s-r), A=(r,s), the lower-right circle center is C2=(s-r,r), and B=(s,r). Since the two circles are externally tangent at O, C1C2=2r; also O is the midpoint of C1C2, hence O=(s/2,s/2). From C1C2=2r, get sqrt(2)(s-2r)=2r. Now compute vectors OA=(r-s/2,s/2) and OB=(s/2,r-s/2). Let t=s/2-r. The tangency equation gives sqrt(2)t=s/2-t, so t/(s/2)=sqrt(2)-1. Thus OA has direction 112.5 degrees from the positive x-axis and OB has direction -22.5 degrees, so the smaller angle AOB is 135 degrees.
